providers.title: Reversible evaluation
providers.scope: A Boolean circuit with s gates for f: {0,1}^m -> {0,1}^k gives a circuit of at most 4s + k gates from NOT, CNOT and Toffoli mapping |x, 0^s, z> to |x, 0^s, z xor f(x)>. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Unrolling a Turing machine computation
providers.scope: A function computed by a Turing machine within T steps has a Boolean circuit of at most c(T+1)^2 gates, written down in time polynomial in m + T. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Exact dyadic sampling
providers.scope: A flag that is 1 with probability exactly A/2^T, computed from a classical label in polynomial time, is appended by a polynomial-size circuit over the fixed gate set. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Retained records
providers.scope: A procedure of polynomially many gates chosen by classical data, measurements and classical computations is a polynomial-size uniform circuit over the gate set with the same distribution of its classical data; its inverse is a circuit over the gate set. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: One step of amplification
providers.scope: If |Pi psi|^2 = 1/4 for psi = V|0>, then (2|psi><psi| - I)(I - 2 Pi) psi = 2 Pi psi, a unit vector in the range of Pi. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Exact quantum factoring (OpenAI)
providers.scope: A polynomial-time uniform family of polynomial-size circuits over one fixed finite gate set outputs the complete prime factorization of every N >= 2 with probability one; proved in the sixth lesson. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Overlaps of the phase register
providers.scope: For every integer D, <chi|T_D|chi> = g(D/Q), where g interpolates exp(-2 pi i z) linearly between the quarter-integers. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A transform with a piecewise-linear phase
providers.scope: A circuit over the gate set of size polynomial in b has the matrix Q^(-1/2) g(kx/Q), Q = 2^b, on a designated success outcome of its auxiliary qubits. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Recovering labels
providers.scope: For Q = B^16 the bins k(d,j) of the reduced fractions j/d with d < B are distinct, and continued fractions decide in polynomial time whether a given k is such a bin and find (d,j). No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Order sampling with the transform
providers.scope: At the true order r, the probability of success and output k(r,j) is the sum over t < r of P(r,j,t). No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Residue-class sums
providers.scope: P(d,j,t) is a dyadic rational computable in polynomial time, |P(d,j,t) - J(jt mod d)| <= 32/Q, and 1/(8d) <= |I(u)| <= 1/d. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A dyadic majorant with an exact sum
providers.scope: There are dyadic U(d,j,u) with 0 <= U(d,j,jt mod d) - P(d,j,t) <= 128/Q and 1/(128d) <= S(d,j) <= 2, where S(d,j) is half their sum and is computed in polynomial time without enumerating the d terms. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: An order trial with prescribed probability (OpenAI)
providers.scope: A uniform quantum trial of polynomial cost returns no candidate or a multiple d < B of the order r of a unit, and returns d = r with probability exactly phi(r) 2^(-ceil(log2 r) - 10), without using r. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A deterministic primality test
providers.scope: A deterministic algorithm decides whether 2 <= m < 2^n is prime in a number of bit operations polynomial in n >= 128, with the congruences (X + a)^m = X^m + a modulo m and X^s - 1 for a prime s <= n^8 and 1 <= a <= 8s. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: An auxiliary prime
providers.scope: For n >= 128 and 2 <= m < 2^n there is a prime s <= n^8 not dividing m with ord_s(m) > n^2. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Composites fail the test
providers.scope: The test rejects every composite m: the values at a root of unity of order s of products of the tested linear factors would be at least 8^(h-1) and fewer than 2^(2h) in number. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Orders from factorizations
providers.scope: Given the factorization of phi(m), the order of a unit modulo m and its factorization are computed with fewer than 2n modular powerings. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Unequal two-adic levels are frequent
providers.scope: For odd m with at least two prime factors, the units whose orders at the prime-power components have unequal 2-adic valuations number F(m) = phi(m) - sum_t prod_i c_i(t) >= phi(m)/2. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Splitting by the order
providers.scope: For a unit a with unequal levels and order r, r is even and gcd(a^(r/2) - 1, m) is a divisor of m other than 1 and m. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A factoring process with verifiable transition probabilities (OpenAI)
providers.scope: A process with exactly L = n^10 transition slots either aborts or generates the occurrence tree D(N); from D(N) one computes for every transition a test for good outputs, a canonical output and the exact dyadic probability s >= 1 - 2^(-2n) of a good output; good outputs always complete the run. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Dyadic completion
providers.scope: A transition with good-output probability s is filtered, with a rare uniform guess that must equal one good output, to pass with any dyadic probability z <= (1 - delta)s exactly. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Known probability from deferred filters (OpenAI)
providers.scope: A polynomial-size preparation succeeds with probability exactly (1 - 2^(-n))^(n^10) and outputs the prime factorization of N on success. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A quarter of success
providers.scope: A polynomial-size uniform circuit has success probability exactly 1/4 and holds the prime factorization of N in its output register on every successful branch. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review
